output.body:
# Link token generation – Call Back API

## In plain words

After you [ask for a link token](/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m2/endpoints/m2-abdm-link-token-hip/01-m2-post-v3-token-generate-token), ABDM answers on your bridge at `/api/v3/hip/token/on-generate-token`. The path is relative to the callback URL you registered. On success the body carries the `linkToken` for the patient's [ABHA address](/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#abha-address). On failure it carries an `error`.

## Before you start

A callback URL registered for your bridge and reachable from the public internet.

## What happens

ABDM posts with the `REQUEST-ID`, `TIMESTAMP` and `X-HIP-ID` headers. The body carries `abhaAddress`, `response` and either `linkToken` or `error`.

## When it goes wrong

`ABDM-1027`: blocked, try again after 24 hours. `ABDM-1051` (Invalid ABHA Number or ABHA Address): check the details you sent. `ABDM-1024` (Dependent service unavailable): try again later.

spec.description:
This API endpoint is used to generate a link token which will be valid for 6 months.. This token can be utilized for Health Information Provider (HIP) Initiated Linking, enabling HIPs to securely link patient health records to their ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) address. The generated token ensures that the linking process is authenticated and authorized, maintaining the integrity and security of health information exchange. This functionality is crucial for facilitating seamless and efficient linking of health records within the healthcare ecosystem.
  1. Authorization: We are passing the access-token in the authorization [Example: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCIgOiAiSldUIiwia2lkIiA6ICJBbFJiNVd]

parameters.description: Unique UUID for track the end to end request transaction
parameters.name: REQUEST-ID

parameters.description: Actual time of the request was initiated, ISO 8601 represents date and time by starting with the year, followed by the month, the day, the hour, the minutes, seconds and milliseconds
parameters.name: TIMESTAMP

parameters.description: Suffix of the consent manager to which the request was intended
parameters.name: X-CM-ID

parameters.description: Identifier of the health information provider to which the request was intended
parameters.name: X-HIP-ID

schema.description: In the request body, either 'abhaNumber' or 'abhaAddress' must be included, with atleast one being mandatory based on the patient profile.

abhaAddress.description: abhaAddress of the user/patient. Allows alpha numeric character and special characters like ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.]+[a-zA-Z0-9]@(abdm|sbx)$

abhaNumber.description: it can be null if abhaNumber is not linked with abhaAddress. Allows numeric character like ^\d{14}$

gender.description: Allows M, F, O, D, T, U as a input

name.description: Only alphabets and special characters like ',.- are allowed like ^[a-zA-Z]+(([',. -][a-zA-Z ])?[a-zA-Z]*)*$

yearOfBirth.description: Year of birth must be 4 digit, ranging between 1900 and 2200

error.description: The error code and message, if any occurred.

code.description: ABDM-1035 - Invalid HIP ID. May be returned either bare (`ABDM-1035`) or with a trailing ": " separator (`ABDM-1035: `); match on the code itself and tolerate the separator.
900902 - Unauthorized. May be returned either bare or with a trailing ": " separator; match on the code itself and tolerate the separator.

description.example: Invalid Credentials. Make sure your API invocation call has a header: 'Authorization : Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' or 'Authorization : Basic ACCESS_TOKEN' or 'apikey: API_KEY'

404.description: server cannot find the requested resource

code.description: 900900 - Unclassified Authentication Failure. May be returned either bare or with a trailing ": " separator; match on the code itself and tolerate the separator.

description.example: Access failure for API: /hiecm/api/v3, version: v3 status: (900900) - Unclassified Authentication Failure

code.description: ABDM-1024 - Dependent service unavailable. May be returned either bare (`ABDM-1024`) or with a trailing ": " separator (`ABDM-1024: `); match on the code itself and tolerate the separator.

reply.Text:
The callback includes the **`REQUEST-ID`** header (which ABDM echoes back) and the **`abhaAddress`** in the response body—either of these lets you match it to the patient.

**Option 1: Use REQUEST-ID** (recommended for async workflows)  
When you call `POST /api/hiecm/v3/token/generate-token`, you create a unique `REQUEST-ID` header. Store that ID with your patient record. When the callback arrives with the same `REQUEST-ID`, you can look up which patient it's for.

**Option 2: Use abhaAddress**  
The callback body includes the `abhaAddress` you sent in the original request, so you can query your database for that address to find the patient.

See the **[Link token generation callback](https://abdm-dev-portal.nha.gov.in/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m2/endpoints/m2-callbacks/01-m2-post-v3-hip-token-on-generate-token)** page for the full callback schema.
